  3. The QuickJS C API on the Odin runtime (src/engine/jscapi)

#The QuickJS C API on the Odin runtime (src/engine/jscapi)

Wren's glue (native/js/odin, package wj and the domains above it) is written against the QuickJS‑ng C API: JSValue words, JS_DupValue/JS_FreeValue, classes with an opaque pointer and a finalizer, JS_NewCFunction2, JS_Call… jscapi implements that API on src/engine/jsrt, so the glue runs on the Odin engine without touching a domain file. It is the only engine now (WJ_JSRT :: true, wj/backend.odin): the QuickJS-ng C engine is gone since 0.6.0.

domain files (web_url.odin, dom_core.odin, …)        unchanged
   wj.JS_Call, wj.JS_NewObject …                     the layer's names
       wj/backend_jsrt.odin                          aliases of src/engine/jscapi
           src/engine/jscapi (167 procedures, "c")  the QuickJS contracts
               src/engine/jsrt                       the engine

The API types (Context, Runtime, Class_Def, Native, Property_Descriptor, …) are defined once, in jscapi/types.odin, and wj aliases them.

#Contracts kept

  • JSValue is the 64‑bit NaN‑boxed word of QuickJS on wasm32 (types.odin: tags -9 … 8, floats offset by 0x7ff8000A << 32, heap values a 32‑bit pointer). The glue's own bit operations (wj.tag_of, is_string, int_of, …) keep working. A 64‑bit host must keep the engine below 4 GiB (the judge's test reserves an arena at a low address); wasm32 has 32‑bit pointers anyway.
  • Counted references on a tracing collector. A reference the caller owns (every JS_New*, JS_Get*, JS_To*, JS_Dup* result) adds one to the ext count in the cell header, which makes the cell a collector root; JS_FreeValue removes it. Values the callee consumes (JS_SetPropertyStr's value, JS_Throw's, JS_DefinePropertyValue*'s, JS_SetModuleExport's …) are released for the caller. Borrowed values (a native's argv, this) carry no count. Natives return an owned value; the bridge releases it as the engine takes it over. Freeing a value that has no count is harmless.
  • Cycles through opaque data are collected. Class_Def.gc_mark reports the values the opaque data holds (JS_MarkValue); the collector subtracts them from the host counts before marking, so an object that holds a counted reference to a closure that captures the object dies (checked by judge capi: 1000 such cycles are all finalized by one JS_RunGC). Finalizers run before any cell of the collection is freed.
  • Classes (JS_NewClassID, JS_NewClass, JS_NewObjectProtoClass, JS_GetOpaque/SetOpaque, and QuickJS-ng's JS_GetAnyOpaque: the class and the opaque data in one call, what the glue reads of every platform object) with all seven JSClassExoticMethods (get/set/has/delete/define/own‑names/own‑property); an exotic get_property replaces the prototype walk after the own shape lookup, as in QuickJS. Wren's own JS_NewObjectProtoClassPayload(ctx, proto, class, size) makes the opaque data size zeroed bytes of the engine's heap in the block of the object's host part, freed with the object (the glue's wrappers: one allocation from the engine's size classes instead of two, and nothing for the finalizer to free). Such an object is made unmarked: the collector does not call its class's gc_mark for it until Wren's JS_SetOpaqueMarked(ctx, obj, true), which the glue calls before the data takes a value (a group, a listener, a [SameObject] value, an impl); a collection then skips the thousands of node wrappers that carry nothing. One the host forgot to mark keeps what its data counts as roots (a leak, not an early free).
  • Native functions: JS_NewCFunction2/3, JS_NewCFunctionData/2, with prototypes generic, generic_magic, constructor, constructor_or_func (and _magic), getter, setter.
  • Errors: the JS_Throw*Error family takes printf arguments (%s %d %u %x %c %.*s %ld); a C caller passes them as wasm32 varargs, which the exported versions read (cexport.odin).
  • Entry points bracket their work with host_enter/host_exit, so the temporaries of an API call made outside any JavaScript (a host event) are released when it returns.
  • Hooks: interrupt handler, GC prologue, rejection tracker, compile‑strings hook, dynamic‑import hook, module normalize/loader/attribute check, JS_SetCanBlock, JS_SetMemoryLimit, GC threshold (and floor). Wren's own JS_SetGCEpilogue is called at the end of every collection, after its finalizers (the glue unpins the nodes of the wrappers they finalized in one call to the browser).
  • Strings read in place: Wren's own JS_ToStringView(ctx, &len, val) gives the bytes of a string value that is all ASCII (a rope flattened first), with no copy and nothing to free, nil for anything else: not NUL-terminated, valid while the value lives (the glue's STR_VIEW: the generated bindings' string arguments, read by the import before the native returns).
  • Modules: JS_NewCModule + JS_AddModuleExport + JS_SetModuleExport (init run before the first import), JS_LoadModule(WithFuncs), JS_ResolveModule, JS_GetModuleRequest*, JS_GetImportMeta, EVAL_FLAG_WREN_NO_RESOLVE.
  • Buffers: JS_NewArrayBuffer adopts host memory (released through realloc_func(…, 0) on collection), copies, JS_NewUint8Array*, JS_GetArrayBuffer, JS_GetTypedArrayBuffer, detach, immutable.
  • JS_WriteObject/JS_ReadObject of bytecode: a function compiled with COMPILE_ONLY keeps its image (Compile_Request.keep_image), so the realm snapshot of qjs_realm.odin / prelude.odin works.

With -define:JSCAPI_EXPORT=true every procedure is also exported under its QuickJS name, for C that calls the API. The build has no such C any more.

#Numbers (when the API was written)

Distinct JS_* / js_* names the glue references: 176.

count
provided by jscapi167
static inline of quickjs.h reimplemented in wj (unchanged)4
helper names of the glue that are not API (js_str, js_cstr …)5
missing0

The API itself is tested natively by judge capi (61 checks); the glue runs on it in every build.

#What is approximated or absent (by weight)

  1. Atoms are permanent (JS_FreeAtom is a no‑op): a page that builds millions of distinct property names keeps them. QuickJS frees them.
  2. JS_WriteObject/JS_ReadObject of data (the structured clone format with REFERENCE): absent; web_clone.odin reads with it (READ_OBJ_REFERENCE) — the clone path must use its own walk.
  3. JS_DefineHostAutoInitProperty makes the value at definition time (correct, not lazy: IndexedDB's interfaces are built in every realm that defines them).
  4. Direct eval from the API (EVAL_TYPE_DIRECT) behaves as an indirect eval (the script eval(…) operator is unaffected).
  5. JS_LoadModule returns the namespace promise through the dynamic‑import job; the layer's own wren module graph fetcher is exercised by LoadModuleWithFuncs only structurally.
  6. JS_IsUncatchableError looks at the last created runtime (no context argument).
  7. JS_ComputeMemoryUsage fills the totals only (malloc_size, counts).
  8. Class call hooks (callable platform objects) are not supported.
  9. Performance: each API call enters/leaves the host bracket and copies the Odin context (the engine's own speed is in runtime.md).
  10. Memory: a tracing heap holds garbage until the next collection (1.6× QuickJS on allocation‑heavy scripts); JS_SetGCGrowth says when the next collection comes (javascript.gc_heap_growth_percent, javascript.gc_min_growth_bytes).
  11. The ownership model is the most likely source of defects (a missing JS_FreeValue leaks a root, an extra one lets a value die early): a debug counter of ext per cell is easy to add in ext_ref/ext_unref.

#Testing

judge capi (src/engine/jsrt/judge/capi_test.odin) runs the API natively on a heap below 4 GiB: values, strings, properties, native functions with data and magic, formatted exceptions, classes with opaque data, cycles through gc_mark, counted references as roots, the GC epilogue (once a collection, after its finalizers), strings read in place (ASCII and concatenations; none of Latin-1, UTF-16 or other values), opaque data in the object's block (zeroed, one per object, cycles through it collected, 10 000 made and dropped without the heap keeping them; JS_GetAnyOpaque of it, of a built-in object, of a number; gc_mark not called until JS_SetOpaqueMarked, the counted values roots until then), exotic objects, promises and jobs, adopted buffers, a native module imported by a script module, a compiled function written out and read back, and a soak of 20 000 temporaries that must be collected.
